'''Alexandra Martha Zoya Slawin''' (born 1961) is a British chemist and professor at the [[University of St Andrews]]. Her research looks to understand the structure of [[Supramolecular assembly|supramolecular]] systems (e.g. rotaxanes and catenanes). She is generally considered as one of the world's leading crystallographers. She was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2011.

== Early life and education ==
Slawin studied chemistry at [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Molecules |url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/molecules/special_issues/Alexandra_Slawin |access-date=2023-03-24 |website=www.mdpi.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2013-08-19 |title=Alexandra M. Z. Slawin |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.201301619 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |language=en |volume=52 |issue=34 |pages=8786 |doi=10.1002/anie.201301619|url-access=subscription }}</ref> After earning her [[bachelor's degree]] she worked at Imperial as an Experimental Officer on [[X-ray crystallography]]. She moved to the [[Loughborough University]], where she completed a PhD on the crystal structures of organic and inorganic systems.<ref name=":0">{{Cite thesis |title=The X-ray crystal structures of organic and inorganic systems |url=https://repository.lboro.ac.uk/articles/thesis/The_X-ray_crystal_structures_of_organic_and_inorganic_systems/9395945/1 |publisher=Loughborough University |date=1997-01-01 |degree=thesis |language=en |first=Alexandra M. Z. |last=Slawin}}</ref> She demonstrated how useful single cyrstal X-ray measurements were to better understand the structures of organic and inorganic solid-state systems.<ref name=":0" /> Toward the end of her thesis she started to focus on [[supramolecular chemistry]], particularly macrocycles, rotaxanes and catenanes.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
Slawin joined the [[University of St Andrews]] in 1999.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=James |date=2022-03-08 |title=The changing nature of research environments |url=https://rse.org.uk/the-changing-nature-of-research-environments/ |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=Royal Society of Edinburgh |language=en-GB}}</ref> She was made a professor in 2004, and serves as the director of the Molecular Structure Lab. Her lab have sophisticated fully automated instrumentation for X-Ray Diffraction, including two rotating anodes and sensitive detectors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof Alexandra Slawin - School of Chemistry |url=https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/chemistry/people/amzs/ |access-date=2023-03-24 |website=www.st-andrews.ac.uk}}</ref> She called the system the Standard (St Andrews Automated Robotic Diffractometer), which she commercialised with [[Rigaku]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Ball |first=Philip |date=2010-05-27 |title=Column: The crucible |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/opinion/column-the-crucible/3005036.article |access-date=2023-03-24 |website=Chemistry World }}</ref>

Slawin is one of the most frequent contributors to the [[Cambridge Crystallographic Database]], having submitted over 3,500 entries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CSD Heroes: Alexandra Martha Zoya Slawin {{!}} CCDC |url=https://www.ccdc.cam.ac.uk/discover/blog/csd-heroes-alexandra-martha-zoya-slawin/ |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=www.ccdc.cam.ac.uk}}</ref> Slawin was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2011. The [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] named her one of their Golden Authors in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celebrating our Golden Authors: Prof. Alexandra Slawin – Dalton Transactions Blog |url=https://blogs.rsc.org/dt/2021/08/04/celebrating-our-golden-authors-prof-alexandra-slawin/ |access-date=2023-03-24 |language=en-US}}</ref>
